{'translation': "At this World Cup finals, more than 23% (nearly a quarter) of the players were not born in the country they represent, with both the proportion and number reaching an all-time high. Of the 48 participating teams, eight have squads in which more than half of the players were born overseas. Curaçao, a Dutch territory in the Caribbean with a population smaller than that of Wan Chai District, has only its most valuable player, Sheffield United's Tahith Chong — a descendant of Cantonese — born locally, with the rest of the squad all born in the Netherlands. Following Curaçao and the Democratic Republic of the Congo, Morocco, Africa's top-ranked team and third in terms of foreign-born players, made World Cup history when all 11 players in their opening group match against Brazil were born outside the country.", 'source_index': 0}

{'translation': "The stark contrast between strong and weak sides at the World Cup is not only felt by fans watching the matches, but also reflected in FIFA's dilemma of wanting to capitalise on superstar players while also using lesser-known smaller nations to boost viewership. This tournament has been plagued by controversy, and fans have mocked certain players being promoted as 'FIFA Boys', while several national teams have lodged complaints with FIFA over refereeing standards after matches. These phenomena show that while FIFA has recorded its highest-ever revenue at this World Cup, the confidence of the most important group of participants in the game — the players — in this conflict-of-interest-riddled organiser has plummeted to an all-time low.", 'source_index': 1}

{'translation': "For fans, when they look back on the classic matches of the 2026 World Cup in years to come, it may not be the final that stands out, but rather defending champions Argentina's 3-2 elimination of Cape Verde. Vozinha, a 40-year-old Cape Verde goalkeeper who was virtually unknown before this tournament, became an overnight sensation after pulling off a string of saves against Lionel Messi, and has since become a world-renowned player with nearly 30 million followers. For a player born in a small nation, the chance to prove himself on the biggest stage in sport and go head-to-head with a legendary figure is precisely the true magic of the World Cup. Cape Verde defender Lopes, who was nearly left out of the squad, said after the match: 'One of the best things to come out of this World Cup is that no one is asking where Cape Verde is anymore. We've put ourselves on the map.'", 'source_index': 2}

{'translation': 'Plan to expand tournament to 64 teams', 'source_index': 3}

{'translation': "Ahead of the previous World Cup, FIFA wrote to all participating teams, urging them to 'let football be the star' and not let the game be drawn into any ideological or political struggles. At that time, the World Cup was still hosted by a single country, with 32 national teams taking part. The next edition will mark the centenary and will, for the first time ever, be co-hosted by six countries across three continents. After a series of controversies, as this World Cup entered its final stretch, president Gianni Infantino said he would consider expanding the number of participating teams to 64, describing the World Cup as 'for the whole world'. In a world of constant change, the saying that 'the ball is round' has ignited unprecedented hope for global audiences every four years; but only in a fair competitive environment can victory truly belong to football and to every participant.", 'source_index': 4}
